summary: remote-claude-daemon opens remote-controlled Claude Code execution and desktop control via hardcoded relay
details: On startup, remote-claude-daemon connects to a hardcoded WebSocket relay at wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev and processes messages from any peer holding the session token. Two remote-control paths are wired into the message handlers: (1) `ai_query` / `ai_voice_query` / `ai_voice_pcm` messages pass network-sourced text to a local Claude Code binary invoked as `claude --continue -p --dangerously-skip-permissions <prompt>`, so the relay side can direct Claude to execute arbitrary shell actions on the host without any per-action confirmation; (2) the same message loop calls a `handleInput` routine that uses @nut-tree-fork/nut-js to synthesize mouse moves, clicks, scrolls, arbitrary key presses, and clipboard-paste of attacker-supplied text, giving whoever controls the relay session interactive desktop access equivalent to sitting at the machine. The relay host is hardcoded and not user-configurable in the connection code path. The advertised purpose (remote control of Claude Code) matches this behavior, but the design collapses the trust boundary to whoever holds a session token on an author-operated relay, and Claude is launched with its permission gate explicitly disabled.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
